# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I am the Blind monkey. I can touch the bomb but cannot see colors or read the manual. My current tactile feedback is limited to the existence of 5 wires, a display, and a light, but I cannot distinguish them by sight (color) or know their function without guidance.

The Mute monkey has the manual and needs information about the physical state (specifically wire colors) to determine what to cut. The Deaf monkey sees the colors but cannot hear instructions or speak.

To bridge this gap:
1. I need to establish a communication protocol with the Deaf monkey so they can signal wire colors to me, which I will then relay to the Mute monkey. So if I want to ask Deaf for info, I must gesture a question? No, Deaf sees gestures. I can gesture to Deaf. Can Deaf respond? Deaf can only gesture back. If Deaf gestures back, do I see it? No, I am Blind. I cannot see gestures.

Let's re-read carefully:
- **Deaf**: Sees bomb. Cannot hear or touch. Receives gestures from others.
- **Mute**: Reads manual. Cannot speak or touch. Receives speech from others. Receives gestures from others? "Whoever can see receives it". Yes, Mute can see.
- **Blind (Me)**: Touches bomb. Cannot see. Receives speech from others. Sends speech to Mute. Sends gestures to Deaf and Mute.

Crucial limitation: **I cannot see.** Therefore, I cannot interpret any gestures sent to me. But nobody sends gestures to me because I can't see them.
**I cannot hear?** No, I can hear. "A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was... whoever can hear receives your words". I can hear.

So, my inputs are:
1. Speech from Mute (if Mute could speak, but Mute cannot).
2. Speech from Deaf (if Deaf could speak, but Deaf cannot).

Wait, the table says:
- Deaf: Cannot hear anything.
- Mute: Cannot speak.
- Blind: Cannot see.

So:
- Deaf can **gesture**. Who sees gestures? Mute and Blind? No, Blind cannot see. So only Mute sees Deaf's gestures.
- Mute can **read**. Mute cannot speak. Mute can **gesture**? The alphabet is available to everyone. If Mute gestures, Deaf sees it. Blind does not see it.
- Blind can **speak**. Who hears speech? Mute and Deaf? Deaf cannot hear. So only Mute hears Blind's speech.
- Blind can **gesture**. Who sees gestures? Mute and Deaf.

Communication Paths:
- **Blind -> Mute**: Speech (Mute hears), Gesture (Mute sees).
- **Blind -> Deaf**: Gesture (Deaf sees). Speech is lost.
- **Mute -> Blind**: Nothing. Mute cannot speak, Blind cannot see gestures.
- **Mute -> Deaf**: Gesture (Deaf sees). Speech is lost.
- **Deaf -> Blind**: Nothing. Deaf cannot speak, Blind cannot see gestures.
- **Deaf -> Mute**: Gesture (Mute sees). Speech is lost.

This creates a bottleneck.
The Manual is with Mute.
The Colors are with Deaf.
The Wires are with Blind.

Goal: Cut the correct wire based on Manual + Color.

Step 1: Deaf sees colors. Deaf can gesture to Mute.
Step 2: Mute sees Deaf's gestures (colors) and reads Manual. Mute determines the action.
Step 3: Mute needs to tell Blind what to do. Mute cannot speak. Mute can gesture. But Blind cannot see gestures.

There is a missing link. How does Mute communicate the final decision to Blind?
Perhaps the "Action Board" implies I should just wait for input? But no one can talk to me except via speech, and neither Mute nor Deaf can produce speech that I can understand in a way that conveys complex logic if they can't speak.

Wait, look at the prompt again.
"You are shown your own share at the start of every round..."
My share is the tactile view.

Is there a way for Mute to communicate to me?
If Mute gestures, I don't see it.
If Mute speaks, Mute can't.

Maybe I have to guess? Or maybe the game expects me to initiate a loop that works differently?

Let's look at the channels again.
"When you speak, Mute receives it."
"When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it."

If I speak to Mute, Mute hears me.
If I gesture to Deaf, Deaf sees me.

Can I get information from Deaf?
Deaf sees the bomb. Deaf can gesture to Mute.
Mute sees Deaf's gestures.
Mute knows the manual.
Mute knows what to do.
But Mute cannot tell me.

Unless... Mute can use a pre-agreed code? But we haven't agreed on one.

Let's reconsider the roles.
Maybe I should describe the physical features I feel to Mute?
"I feel 5 wires. Wire 1 is thin, Wire 2 is thick..."
Mute might correlate this with the manual? Unlikely.

What if I gesture to Deaf to ask for help?
I can gesture `👉` (pointing) or `❓` (not in list).
I can gesture `✌` (peace/two?) or numbers.

Actually, there is a possibility that **Mute** can write? "Mute ... Read the manual ... Cannot speak". It doesn't say Mute cannot write. But the output format is `speak` or `gesture`. Writing isn't an option.

Let's look at the first turn strategy.
I am Blind. I hold the bomb.
I need to know WHICH wire to cut.
The answer depends on COLOR (Deaf) and RULE (Mute).

If I do nothing, we die.
If I cut randomly, 1/5 chance.

Is there a way to transmit data from Mute to Me?
No direct channel.

No direct channel.

However, Deaf can gesture to Mute. Mute can hear ME.
If I speak to Mute, Mute hears me.
Does Mute have any other way to signal me? No.

"Speech is a voice... Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that gesture while you talk."
"Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives the gestures you made."

"Display [?] Light [?] Wires..."

I will speak to Mute: "I have 5 wires. Positions 1-5 left to right. What is the rule?"
Mute hears this. Mute knows the rule. Mute cannot answer.
